children: Iraq has started preparing plans, feasibility studies and cost estimates for a proposed 2 million barrels per day (bpd) cross-border crude oil pipeline system linking Basra with Haditha and onward to Syria's Baniyas and Fishkhabour, the Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.
The project envisages a 56-inch pipeline from Basra to Haditha, from where the system would branch into two routes, North Oil Company Director General Faisal Hamadi Ramadan told INA.

One route would extend from Haditha to Baniyas in Syria, with a planned capacity of 1 million bpd, while the second would connect Haditha to the Iraqi-Turkish pipeline towards Fishkhabour, also with a capacity of 1 million bpd.
The overall pipeline system is expected to extend around 1,000 kilometres (km).
Ramadan said Ministry of Oil committees have started preparing the project's plans, feasibility studies, cost estimates, routes and maps.
He added that companies previously identified for the project have begun meetings with senior Ministry of Oil officials.

Under the latest directive from Iraq's prime minister, procedures will also be completed with extraction companies operating under the Ministry of Oil to establish a contractual framework for the project, he said.
The pipeline is intended to diversify Iraq's crude export routes and reduce its reliance on exports through the Strait of Hormuz and transportation by tanker trucks.
Construction is expected to take 24 to 48 months once the project proceeds, according to Ramadan.
Details about the estimated investment cost, financing and procurement model, targeted tender/contract award dates weren’t disclosed.

Past media reports have indicated that US companies have been roped in for various elements of the project. In July 2026, Iraq and Syria signed a government-to-government Memorandum of Understanding and separate Heads of Agreement with UCC Urbacon Concessions Investments of Qatar, Chevron Business Development EMEA, part of US-based oil giant Chevron and TIC Infra II, part of US-based TI Capital, to advance the cross-border pipeline.
Additionally, Texas-based KBR will provide consultancy services including feasibility studies, technical advisory, and route engineering for the project..
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)
